note: Rewritten from the species-level description in Thakur et al. 1992, the original in English. The original records 2 soldiers and 8 pseudoworkers, the alate UNKNOWN. OCR problems: in Table 4 the head height is printed 0.65—0.58 (an inverted range) and the stylus length as 0.8 mm; both are copied as printed and noted.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule and antennae pale yellow to reddish yellowish brown; antennae the same colour as the head capsule; labrum yellowish brown to brown, the frontal region slightly paler; mandibles light brown to dark reddish brown; legs creamy yellow to rusty brown; the rest paler than the head capsule. Head capsule and thorax sparsely hairy, abdomen moderately hairy, each tergite with a row of hairs along its posterior margin; body length about 4.70—4.85 mm. Head capsule nearly rectangular, distinctly longer than wide, widest in the posterior third, the sides nearly parallel to the antennal socket bases and very slightly converging forwards; posterior lateral corners rounded, posterior margin convex; frons inclined forwards and slightly concave in the middle; dorsal lateral protuberances not very distinct. Y suture indistinct. Fontanelle absent. Eyes small oval white spots, flush with the head capsule, greatest diameter 0.13—0.15 mm; ocelli indistinct. Antennae 9—10-segmented, segment 1 largest, segment 2 columnar, about 1.5 times segment 3, segment 3 shortest, segment 4 nearly as long as segment 2 but wider, the segments from the 5th onwards pyriform and gradually longer, the terminal segment narrower than the preceding one. Anteclypeus nearly trapezoidal, longer than the postclypeus, translucent, nearly rectangular; postclypeus nearly rectangular, separated from the frontal region only by a shallow groove. Labrum broadly ligulate, slightly wider than long, sides weakly convex, anterior margin nearly straight, hairy. Mandibles short and stout, slightly shorter than half the head length (mandible-head index 0.47—0.49), moderately incurved at the tip, with a distinct basal swelling; left mandible with 3 marginal teeth (the 1st and 2nd close together in the apical third, the 3rd in the middle of the basal half), right mandible with 2 marginal teeth in the middle. Postmentum clavate, greatest width near the apical quarter, narrowing posteriorly into a narrow waist and slightly narrowing anteriorly; anterior margin nearly straight, posterior margin convex and raised in the middle. Pronotum nearly rectangular, narrower than the head width, anterior margin broadly concave in the middle, anterior lateral corners broadly rounded, sides weakly convex and converging posteriorly, posterior margin weakly convex with a very shallow median concavity; mesonotum slightly wider than the pronotum, posterior lateral corners rounded, posterior margin weakly convex; metanotum as wide as the mesonotum, posterior lateral corners rounded, posterior margin convex. Legs short and stout, tibial spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen long and hairy, the 10th segment not very sclerotized; cerci 2-segmented, about 0.08—0.10 mm long; styli single-segmented, about 0.08 mm long.

sections.text: Soldier measurements (Table 4, 2 specimens; range and mean, mm): body length 4.70—4.85 (4.78); head length including the mandibles 1.68—1.80 (1.72); head length to the mandible base 1.18—1.28 (1.23); greatest head width 0.90—0.95 (0.93); head height 0.65—0.58 (0.66, as printed); head index I (width/length) 0.74—0.76 (0.75); left mandible length 0.58—0.60 (0.59); right mandible length 0.55—0.60 (0.58); mandible-head index I 0.47—0.49 (0.48); postmentum least (median) length 0.70—0.80 (0.75); postmentum greatest width 0.33; postmentum least width 0.20—0.24 (0.22); pronotum length 0.40—0.50 (0.45); pronotum greatest width 0.75—0.90 (0.83); pronotum index 0.52—0.56 (0.54).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Pseudoworker: head capsule creamy yellow, antennae brownish, postclypeus and labrum more sclerotized and brownish. Head capsule and body moderately hairy; body length about 3.50—4.70 mm. Head capsule semicircular, wider than long, widest in the posterior third, sides weakly convex and slightly converging forwards, posterior lateral corners rounded, posterior margin convex; fontanelle and ocelli absent; eyes almost indiscernible, a small oval spot on each side. Antennae 9—10-segmented, segment 1 largest, segment 2 columnar and narrower than segment 1 (with 9 segments, segment 2 wider and longer than segment 3 and segment 4 shortest; with 10 segments, segment 2 almost twice as long as segment 3 and segment 3 narrowest and shortest), the remaining segments gradually longer and wider, the terminal segment oval and narrower than the preceding one. Anteclypeus a narrow band, raised in the middle; postclypeus nearly rectangular, darker than the frontal region, separated by a ridge. Labrum shovel-shaped, wider than long, the sides converging towards the broadly rounded anterior margin. Mandibles of the typical Glyptotermes type. Pronotum nearly rectangular, wider than long, distinctly narrower than the head capsule, anterior margin truncate, broadly concave and with a very weak median notch, posterior margin with a distinct median notch; mesonotum slightly wider than the pronotum, posterior margin weakly convex; metanotum wider than the mesonotum, posterior margin weakly convex. Legs as in the soldier. Abdomen spherical, hairy, cerci 2-segmented and about 0.08—0.10 mm long, styli single-segmented (given as 0.8 mm in the original).
